problem:
Let the vectors $v$ and $w$ be orthogonal. 
If $|u\cdot v{|}^{2}+2‖v+w{‖}^{2}=158$ and $‖u‖=‖w‖=5$, then what is the minimum possible value of $‖v‖?$
worked_solution:
First, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, simplifying, and substituting in the given information, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}158 & ={|u\cdot v|}^{2}+2‖v+w{‖}^{2} \\  & \le {‖u{‖}^{2}\cdot ‖v‖}^{2}+2‖v+w{‖}^{2} \\  & ={5}^{2}\cdot ‖v{‖}^{2}+2‖v+w{‖}^{2} \\  & =25‖v{‖}^{2}+2‖v+w{‖}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $v⊥w$, using the Pythagorean theorem, simplifying, and substituting in the given information, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}25‖v{‖}^{2}+2‖v+w{‖}^{2} & =25‖v{‖}^{2}+2(‖v{‖}^{2}+‖w{‖}^{2}) \\  & =25‖v{‖}^{2}+2(‖v{‖}^{2}+{5}^{2}) \\  & =27‖v{‖}^{2}+50.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining the two steps above, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}158 & \le 27‖v‖+50 \\ 108 & \le 27‖v{‖}^{2} \\ 4 & \le ‖v{‖}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $4\le ‖v{‖}^{2}$ implies that $2\le ‖v‖.$ Notice that we disregard the negative solutions since the norm can't be negative.

Therefore, the minimum possible value of $‖v‖$ is $2.$
